items.definition: Correctly seizing a device so that evidence is preserved and admissible.
items.examples: Photographing the screen, putting a phone in a Faraday bag, and documenting the chain of custody.
items.examTip: A Faraday bag/cage blocks all signals so the device can't be remotely wiped or communicate. Document chain of custody!
keyFacts: Plan for a range of devices; collect passwords/PINs, chargers/cables
Retain the current power state if possible
Isolate from networks: photograph screen, airplane mode, Faraday bag/cage
Appropriate packaging, document chain of custody, establish legal permissions

items.definition: Taking a forensic image (exact copy) of the system and analysing it with forensic tools.
items.examples: Imaging a drive then reviewing system logs and user activity for evidence of compromise.
items.examTip: You analyse a COPY/image, never the original — this preserves the evidence (link D2.1.3).
keyFacts: Take an image (exact copy) of the system
Use a forensic analysis tool
Review files, settings, system logs and user activity
Analyse malware activity and alerts

items.definition: Difficulties of collecting evidence from a system that is still running.
items.examples: Capturing data in RAM before it is lost when the device is switched off.
items.examTip: Live forensics is tricky because data in active memory (RAM) and temporary files are lost when powered off.
keyFacts: Data changes in situ while the system runs
Recovering/preventing corruption of data
Capturing data in active memory (RAM) and remote data
Not losing temporary files

items.definition: Collecting and analysing evidence from network infrastructure after an incident.
items.examples: Reviewing firewall, router and server logs to trace an attacker's activity.
items.examTip: Always agree methodology and get permission first, and ensure testing won't disrupt the live system.
keyFacts: Agree a methodology with supervisory/investigatory authorities
Get permission; ensure testing won't disrupt the live system
Use passive and active analysis tools
Review firewalls, switches, routers, WAPs and client/server logs

items.definition: Recording the scene of an incident thoroughly and at the time.
items.examples: Taking photos and diagrams of equipment, plus contemporaneous notes and witness statements.
items.examTip: 'Contemporaneous notes' = notes made at the time. These strengthen the reliability of evidence.
keyFacts: Plan for a range of scenarios and secure the scene
Plans, photos and diagrams of the scene
Contemporaneous notes (made at the time)
Witness statements

items.definition: Keeping exact copies/images of the system so they can be compared against a clean original.
items.examples: Taking a physical image of an entire drive and generating a hash to prove it hasn't changed.
items.examTip: A physical image copies the ENTIRE drive (including deleted/temporary files); a targeted image copies only selected files. Physical captures more potential evidence (sample paper Q4c).
keyFacts: Keep originals/a clean system for comparison
Generate a hash/checksum for copies/images to prove integrity
Capture whole disk, files/folders, memory (RAM/BIOS/SIM)
Include temporary files, deleted data and system-generated files

items.definition: Documenting all findings and actions so the evidence is reliable and the chain of custody is intact.
items.examples: Logging every action taken, by whom, with timestamps.
items.examTip: No action should change data on the device; collection must be by a competent person; keep a chain of custody.
keyFacts: No collection/action should change data on the device
Collection by a competent person
Create a trail/record of all actions (chain of custody)
Document who is responsible for collection/decisions

items.definition: Recording any changes — intentional or accidental — made by the investigator, because altered data may be inadmissible.
items.examples: Always working from a copy/image so the original remains untouched.
items.examTip: Altered original data can be ruled inadmissible in court — that's why investigators work with copies/images.
keyFacts: Document all actions from initial seizure
Altered data may be inadmissible
Work with copies/images, not the original device

items.definition: Creating visual evidence of findings, and ensuring evidence is genuine and not a false positive.
items.examples: Screenshots with date-time stamps; manually reviewing alerts to filter out false positives.
items.examTip: High false-positive rates cause 'alert fatigue'. Manual review filters obvious false positives.
keyFacts: Visual evidence: photos, videos, screenshots with timestamps/metadata
Define file signatures and search criteria
Know tool error rates; manually review positives
Avoid alert fatigue from too many false positives

items.term: Evidence of a Crime or Incident
items.definition: Assessing whether findings show a crime, regulatory breach, policy breach or other incident.
items.examples: Findings showing a criminal hack, a GDPR breach, or negligence by staff.
items.examTip: Findings could indicate criminal activity, regulatory/contractual breach, policy non-compliance, a cyber attack or negligence.
keyFacts: Criminal activity or regulatory breach
Civil liability / contractual breach
Non-compliance with internal policy
Cyber attack, negligence or mismanagement

items.definition: Indicators that a system has been compromised internally or externally.
items.examples: Unusual outbound traffic to a foreign region; spikes in failed login attempts; unusual DNS requests.
items.examTip: Indicators of compromise: unusual traffic, unusual logins, unusual DNS/port use, suspicious file changes.
keyFacts: Unusual traffic (inbound/outbound, odd regions, DoS signs)
Unusual login attempts and DNS requests
Increase in file/data reads/requests; unusual port usage
Suspicious changes to files or system data

items.definition: Producing a structured report on the incident and recommending improvements to prevent recurrence.
items.examples: A report with a clear structure analysing what went wrong and recommending policy and training improvements.
items.examTip: Report structure: title, contents, intro, headings, consistent bullets/numbering, conclusions, citations.
keyFacts: Clear structure: title, contents, intro, headings, conclusions, citations
Analyse: errors in procedures/preventative measures, detection delays
Recommend improvements to IT policies
Recommend improvements to physical, software, hardware, process and training measures
